definition: Travesty means a debased and grossly inferior imitation.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word travesty. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know travesty should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Critics called the outdoor 'tennis exhibition' a travesty of the sport—sponge balls, a sagging rope for a net, and scores invented by the announcer.
A copy just reproduces the original, well or badly, with no attitude toward it; a travesty degrades what it imitates.
A spoof pokes affectionate fun and can even flatter its target; a travesty goes further down the same road, debasing the original until the imitation insults it.

A mockery is a version so botched or hollow that it ridicules the very thing it claims to be — a hearing where no one listens makes a mockery of justice. A travesty gets there through imitation: some performance actually exists, and it is so debased it insults its original. Both words need real conduct to point at.

A sham is a fake passed off as the real thing, and it requires no performance at all — the deception can live entirely in the claim. A travesty must actually be carried out: an imitation exists, and it degrades its original. Where nothing was ever done, no imitation exists to judge.
